original_card.question: Can one measured replay bottleneck be sped up without dropping coverage?
methods: Profile one isolated replay and optimize the measured bottleneck.
Design source-bound reuse with explicit dependency invalidation and negative controls.
original_card.acceptance_gate: Report before/after wall time on the same fixture, retained checks and invalidation behavior.

first_step.inspect: Read the selected reproduction command and choose a single replay stage for profiling.
first_step.scope: Positive control / source-bound orientation only; this is not a new construction or full cold replay.

original_card.first_experiment: Measure one unchanged fixture, preserve check coverage, and test one optimization with invalidation controls.
original_card.bottleneck_link: Faster trustworthy replays increase review throughput and let mechanism candidates be checked sooner.
allowed_variations: Profile one stage or design one source-bound cache boundary.
scope_change_triggers: Skipping coverage or comparing different fixtures to claim speedup.

actual_scope: Can scripts/experiments/disjoint_tensor.py:DisjointTensor.verify replace its disjoint-output expected-support genexpr with an equivalent closed-form point-incidence mask (full ^ OR_{p in T} vertex[p]) so verify receipts, dag_sha256 and support require() checks stay fieldwise identical on the historical h=26 circuit?
scope_change_reason: The catalogue card asks for one measured replay bottleneck with before/after wall time and retained checks. Expertise override selected verifier-engineering after ExclusionCircuit support masks (#2001) and SharedPoint digests (#1994) claimed those objects; profiling named DisjointTensor.verify's leave-intersecting-inputs genexpr on the historical h=26 certificate circuit as the next unclaimed hot path.
bottleneck_link: Side result on review throughput: disjoint-tensor-compression, ternary-side, dyadic-central-factor and parity-side certificates call DisjointTensor.verify. A faster identical support check does not change kappa or the binding complex supplier.
stop_rule: Ship an equivalence-preserving DisjointTensor.verify support-mask change with frozen baseline, identical receipts on the historical h=26 circuit, updated source pins only on the four binding certificates, registered replay and a measured before/after median. Do not touch ExclusionCircuit, SharedPoint digests, or run the selected cold frontier replay.
evidence: PASS_DISJOINT_TENSOR_SUPPORT_MASKS via research/disjoint-tensor-support-masks/verify.py (also under -O); PASS_IDENTICAL_DISJOINT_TENSOR_SUPPORT_MASK_RECEIPTS via benchmark.py; four certificates differ from base only in the scripts/experiments/disjoint_tensor.py source pin.
author: Wentao Li
ai_assistance: Substantial AI assistance for orientation, overlap search, profiling, implementation, packaging, benchmarking and writing. Not independent human peer review.

open_questions.question: Is DisjointTensor.verify_frames / frame_data worth a separate identical-receipt rewrite?
open_questions.why_it_matters: On h=26, verify_frames dominates the full certificate wall time (~4s) via point-union loops in frame_data; it is a different object from the verify expected-support path measured here.
open_questions.first_step: Profile DisjointTensor(26).verify_frames alone and check whether ancestor/target-union construction can reuse precomputed incidence without changing transition receipts.
open_questions.blocked_by: Out of this session's stop rule; DisjointTensor.verify support masks were the measured bottleneck.

open_questions.question: Should DisjointTensor.verify's dag_sha256 json.dumps path get a hand-rolled formatter like the mixed-point / SharedPoint digests?
open_questions.why_it_matters: json.dumps is a secondary share of verify after the support genexpr; a byte-identical line writer would be a different object from the closed-form support masks.
open_questions.first_step: Profile the post-mask verify residual and compare a hand-rolled [[i,args,str(support)]] encoder against the committed dag_sha256.
open_questions.blocked_by: Out of this session's stop rule; support masks were the primary measured bottleneck.
